 The Indian Ministry of Defense shared a new strategic vision for the Air Force on Sunday, outlined by the new Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, the 29th Chief of the Air Staff of the Indian Air Force (IAF). He unveiled a concept called ‘VAYU’ that sets out four priorities for the service: operational readiness, domestic defense capabilities, technological innovation and joint operations.
 Dixit began his tenure on 1 November 2026, paying tribute to fallen soldiers at the National War Memorial in New Delhi before receiving a ceremonial Guard of Honor at Air Force Station New Delhi.
 An experimental test pilot and qualified flying instructor, Dixit has more than 3,500 hours of flying experience. His previous appointments include Chief of Integrated Defense Staff to the Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee, Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of Central Air Command and Vice Chief of the Air Staff.
 The ‘VAYU’ framework outlines four pillars of the IAF’s future development. The first, Vigilance, Victory and Readiness, focuses on maintaining operational preparedness and restoring the Air Force’s combat strength to its authorized levels. Aatmanirbharta (self-reliance) calls for accelerating the development of indigenous aircraft, sensors, weapons and other technologies.
 The third pillar, Yukti (innovation), envisages the integration of artificial intelligence into command-and-control systems, the development of counter-drone capabilities and improvements in operational resilience. The final pillar, Unity of Effort, emphasizes closer coordination with the Indian Army, Navy and national agencies.
 According to the Indian government, the vision is intended to guide the Air Force towards greater technological self-reliance, operational readiness and integration with other branches of the country’s armed forces.
